Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: Government-to-person (G2P) payments are active: World Bank note describes Egypt’s Takaful & Karama social transfer payments delivered monthly using program-linked smart cards and e-Finance as government payments network operator; AfricaNenda also lists IPN use case “Social disbursements (G2P)”. ([World Bank ‘G2P Payment Arrangements in Egypt and COVID-19’](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/533491624466169827/pdf/G2P-Payment-Arrangements-in-Egypt-and-COVID-19.pdf);[AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 IPN Egypt case study](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/siips2025/siips_2025_IPN-Egypt_CaseStudy_en.pdf))

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: P2B merchant payments are supported: IPN now facilitates merchant/person-to-business payments and merchants can receive funds instantly via IPN/InstaPay; CBE also launched SoftPOS to allow merchants to accept contactless card payments via smartphones/tablets, expanding acceptance infrastructure. ([AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 IPN Egypt case study](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/siips2025/siips_2025_IPN-Egypt_CaseStudy_en.pdf);[Daily News Egypt on CBE SoftPOS launch](https://www.dailynewsegypt.com/2026/02/01/cbe-launches-soft-pos-service-for-contactless-mobile-payments-to-cut-merchant-costs/))

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: IPN is reported to support “Taxes and fees (P2G)” as a use case; additionally, Egypt has mobile-based government payments channels (e.g., NTRA license for direct carrier billing for government payments like utilities, traffic fines, civil registry). ([AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 IPN Egypt case study](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/siips2025/siips_2025_IPN-Egypt_CaseStudy_en.pdf);[tpay press release on NTRA DCB license for government payments](https://tpaymobile.com/tpay-secures-license-to-offer-direct-mobile-payments-for-government-services-in-egypt/))

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: P2P is supported via IPN/InstaPay (instant transfers between individuals using mobile number/Instant Payment Address and across banks/wallets/cards) and via mobile wallets (NTRA lists peer-to-peer wallet-to-wallet transfers anywhere in Egypt). ([AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 IPN Egypt case study](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/siips2025/siips_2025_IPN-Egypt_CaseStudy_en.pdf);[NTRA Mobile Wallet Services](https://www.tra.gov.eg/en/regulations/consumer-manuals-and-tips/mobile-wallet-services/))

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Partial evidence: Egypt has a general Consumer Protection Law No. 181 of 2018 covering consumer rights including e-commerce; CBE mobile payments regulations referenced by AFI recommend service contracts with transparent terms & conditions, defined rights/obligations, service availability/SLA notices, data confidentiality, and dispute resolution controls for mobile payment services. ([Riad & Riad on Consumer Protection Law 181/2018](https://riad-riad.com/new-egyptian-consumer-protection-law/);[AFI ‘Financial Inclusion through DFS & Fintech: the case of Egypt’](https://www.afi-global.org/sites/default/files/publications/2018-08/AFI_Egypt_Report_AW_digital.pdf))

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: Ad hoc public reporting exists: AfricaNenda reports IPN transaction volumes/values (2022–2024) and unique users, and media reports cite CBE Financial Stability reporting on IPN Q1 2025 volumes/value (263M transactions, >EGP 1.2T). Evidence is not clearly a regular monthly/quarterly public dashboard accessible. ([AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 IPN Egypt case study](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/siips2025/siips_2025_IPN-Egypt_CaseStudy_en.pdf);[ArabFinance citing CBE Financial Stability report](https://www.arabfinance.com/ar/news/newdetails/29811))

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Egypt has high digital account penetration and large active wallet base: CBE reported financial inclusion rate 77.6% (54.7M users with active transaction accounts incl. bank accounts, Egypt Post accounts, mobile wallets, prepaid cards) by end-2025; NTRA reported >50M mobile wallets by end-2024. This is used as proxy for active digital payment users, though not all accounts are necessarily active digital-payment users. ([Ahram Online citing CBE](https://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContentP/3/562552/Business/Egypt%E2%80%99s-financial-inclusion-rate-inches-up-to---by.aspx);[NTRA GSMA index release](https://www.tra.gov.eg/en/the-gsma-global-system-for-mobile-communications-association-has-released-its-annual-regulatory-index-for-mobile-money-for-2024-egypts-national-telecom-regulatory-authority-ntra-advanced/))
